Name: Johan Torres
Question: Do you believe Cyclops made the right decision to abandon Madelyne Pryor and their son in favor of reuniting with Jean Grey in the comics?
Answer: Yes. Obviously it was the right decision. The one thing we know about the relationship between Scott Summers and Madelyne Pryor is that she was physically abusive. If the genders in this story were reversed, it would be a tragic story of a person getting out of an abusive relationship. We know that to be true because every Hank Pym story is still about the one time he hit Janet. It is absolutely baffling to me that people give Maddie a pass on her physical abuse, or even applaud her. Additionally Madelyne Pryor was extremely psychologically abusive. Madelyne Pryor regularly goes behind Scott’s back to his friends and co-workers in order to talk shit about him. She consistently attempts to poison his entire social circle against him, with her ultimate goal being to isolate him in Alaska thousands of miles from his entire support system. It’s incredibly manipulative, incredibly malicious. She will do things like blame Scott for when the Beyonder abducted him, something he has no control over. And let’s talk about the infamous scene where he “abandons” her. All she knows is that Warren needs to see Scott. Warren, not Jean. Hearing that Warren, one of Scott’s three oldest and closest friends needs to see him causes her to end the relationship. Her. Not him. Stop to think about how manipulative this is. How cruel this is. How possessive this is. She won’t even let him see Angel. She is threatened and lashes out to the point of ending her marriage because Scott wants to see Angel. She can’t allow him any relationship with another person. In fact, this pretty much proves that Scott was right to not tell her about Jean. It would be unreasonable to expect him, in this situation, not to see Jean. But she can’t even handle him going to see Warren. It’s so abusive. And none of this includes her selling her soul to a demon, trying to sacrifice her child to a demon, or telepathically manipulating Scott to keep him in the marriage. Or how she cheated on him with his brother. She was always a monster. Long before any of those revelations/retcons. Scott never even wanted to be in the relationship in the first place. He spends the entire time they dated trying to get out of it, and then when they get married keeps trying to end it. The sole reason he stuck it out with her is because everyone kept gaslighting him into staying in what is an obviously toxic relationship with an obviously abusive person. I wish Scott had taken lil’ baby Cable with him. But that’s not something that we can really say is on him, he was getting out of a profoundly abusive relationship. Like I said, I have been baffled by this for years. I do not understand how anyone can think Scott did anything wrong in this relationship, aside from staying in it. We’re literally shown physical abuse on pannel.

Name: Johan Torres
Question: What impact do you think Marvel's decision to end the current volumes of Star Wars and Darth Vader comics will have on the future of Star Wars storytelling?
Answer: In early 2015 Marvel launched their Star Wars line with two ongoing comics, Star Wars and Darth Vader. The next year it would be joined by two more titles, Poe Dameron and Doctor Aphra. Star Wars, Darth Vader, and Doctor Aphra were all set in-between the events of A New Hope and Empire Strikes Back. In 2019, after four years, the entire Star Wars comic line was canceled. In 2020 the Star Wars comics were relaunched with Star Wars, Darth Vader, Doctor Aphra, and Bounty Hunters. This time all the comics were set between Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. I haven’t checked to see if there is any promotional material for upcoming Star Wars comics. But the thing is that Marvel has already canceled the entire line once before. So if I were to bet money, I would bet that Marvel is preparing to relaunch with comics set after Return of the Jedi, and those comics would be Star Wars, Doctor Aphra, and maybe a third title. Also a Darth Vader comic set some time in the past. The current timeframe of the comics is weird and difficult because Han Solo can’t appear. They actually wound up giving him his own comic, Han Solo and Chewbacca, in order to wedge him in somewhere. The decision to periodically reboot the whole line is, to me, not particularly impactful. It’s just saying “here’s where the movie happens.” The content of the comics, however, is going to be extremely impactful. The most obvious example of this is Doctor Aphra. She created just to be a supporting character in the Darth Vader comic (and, likely, to be killed by Vader). She became so popular she, a completely original character not in any movie, helmed two long running comic series and was added to multiple video games and has several toys. Comics are a low cost, low risk way to work out ideas. And so their main impact is in what transfers over to mediums that are exponentially more expensive.

Name: Johan Torres
Question: Have any members of the X-Men ever joined the Avengers? If yes, who were they and what was their role?
Answer: A bunch of them have joined the Avengers. It is not too terribly uncommon for X-Men to, essentially, take a break from mutant issues to join the Avengers. But no matter how much they to be an uncomplicated hero, it catches back up to them. The first member of the X-Men to migrate to the Avengers was Beast. And Beast is really the only character to really get treated as having both teams co-equal. This was after the All New All Different X-Men debuted. And after his solo title got canceled. But before he joined the Defenders, and long before X-Factor. Anyway In Avengers #137, Thor felt the Avengers were understaffed and so made a TV commercial asking for people to join. They didn’t have American Idol back then and so didn’t know how that would actually go in real life. Beast shows up and joins the team. Beast really gets his fun loving goofy personality here. As opposed to the overly erudite studious one in X-Men (though, honestly, frequently silly there too) and his tortured monster routine in his solo title. He becomes really good friends with Wonder Man. And he is on the team for an extremely long time. He eventually leaves in Avengers #211, so it was a good seventy-four issue long stretch. Nearly twenty-five years will pass before the next member of the X-Men joins the Avengers, Wolverine. In New Avengers #6, the New Avengers have a fun little romp in the Savage Land where they run into Wolverine who is also there for some reason. And they ask him to join the team because he will kill people. No, seriously, that’s the reason. This is deeply silly for multiple reasons. And it begins what is one of the more bizarre deconstructions of Wolverine as a character. Where the loner who doesn’t get along with people joins every team he can. In fact, he becomes a cop. You sort of really see how pre-mind wipe Wolverine worked for every single evil government agency that would hire him. New Avengers was a weird book, and not very good. The next X-Man to join was Storm. This is Avengers vol. 4 #19. She’s only there because T’Challa askes her to be there, and he only askes because he wants her to stay in New York where he was at the time. She’s possibly the least committed member of the Avengers ever. Her stint as a member of the Fantastic Four was far more obviously something she actually wanted to do. Then we have the Uncanny Avengers recruits. Havok, Sunspot, Cannonball, Rogue and Sunfire. And, eventually, Cable. Hahaha. No. Cannonball and Sunspot would go on to a much better stint in the Avengers in Johnathan Hickman’s run. That’s where Cannonball meets his wife. Sunspot sticks around even longer with his own Avengers team, culminating in the USAvengers. Which is really fun. So far there has only been one Avenger to make the opposite trip, and that Namor. Namor was established to be a mutant in X-Men #6. And no one did much with that information for decades. But during Dark Reign he and Emma Frost formed an alliance against Norman Osborn, which eventually became an alliance between the X-Men and Atlantis. Namor joins the various X-Men teams for a quite long time.

Question: How come leftists nowadays label people who state facts, e.g. "women are XX men are XY", as "far-right," "conspiracy theorists," "spreaders of disinformation," "Putin lovers," "fascists," and "racists."?
Answer: The most recent example of people saying “women are XX men are XY” was in reference to an Algerian female boxer at the Olympics who they decided looked too manly, and of whom there is still no evidence supporting the idea she even has the XY chromosome. This is within the past month, you know. This is the perfect example of a motte-and-bailey argument. There was a global harassment campaign against Imane Khelif led by some of the richest and most powerful people on the planet, simply based on the fact that they thought she looked too manly. Shrieking, “this thing participating in women’s boxing in the Olympics is a man!” is your bailey, a hard to defend and controversial statement. While “I’m just saying women are XX and men are XY” is your motte. No one cares if you are teaching fifth grade health class and say that women have the XX chromosomes and men have the XY chromosomes, even if that is extremely overly simplistic. You can say that all day long. But you are not teaching health. When you say, “women have the XX chromosomes and men have the XY chromosomes” you are saying it for extremely pointed reasons. Like harassing an Olympic boxer. And it is entirely fair to label you based on the positions you are actually advocating. And it is extremely unfair for you to attempt to decontextualize what you are actually saying, presenting it in its most anodyne and platonic form. Don’t harass Olympic boxers from now on, m’kay?
